Independent review of run r-20260929T131620919074-srw-ingest-service-lasts-and-names-its-paths at head 5e1c4f2a against base 7774c689, the section-5 repair that makes the generated telemetry-ingest script last as a standing service and carry the record and index paths the submitter chose, resolved to absolute paths. Both halves of the goal land and both are independently reproduced at each revision. The change also matches the plan's own decision element for section 5, which names the ingest a standing SLURM service, and it repairs all three findings the preceding review left on the node that built this service. It loses points for two undelivered things and one unpinned value: the evidence fragment its write scope declares was never written, the standing-service rule is pinned by equality with the shared constant rather than by the constant's value, and the test module keeps the two words the commit retyped in the CLI it ships beside.

Goal fidelity. The committed generator now passes time_limit=_SUPPORTING_SERVICE_TIME_LIMIT, the same '0' the router script at slurm.py:927 and the lane-refresher script at slurm.py:1007 already carry, and _SCHEDULED_SERVICE_TIME_LIMIT is deleted with the five-line comment that explained it, leaving no reference to it anywhere in imas_ambix, tests or docs at head. The CLI resolves both paths before generating the script, so the exec line names the absolute target. Driven directly rather than through the node's tests, the dry-run at head prints '#SBATCH --time=0' and 'exec ... agent ingest --record /tmp/probe-qcenipu5/receipts --index /tmp/probe-qcenipu5/watch.sqlite3', where the same probe against the base revision prints '#SBATCH --time=01:00:00' and 'exec ... agent ingest --record receipts --index watch.sqlite3' with the relative arguments unresolved (review-base-script-probe.log, review-head-script-probe.log). Those two readings are the goal, statement by statement.

The previously recorded defects, and whether they still reproduce. This node exists to repair three findings the preceding review recorded against the node that built the ingest service, and this review confirmed each one still reproduced at the base before accepting the repair. The endless loop under a one-hour walltime: base 7774c689 prints '#SBATCH --time=01:00:00' for a script whose emitted command passes no --once. The missing exec-line assertions: with the head test file placed over the base source, tests/test_agent_ingest_cli.py reddens exactly two tests, the first reporting 'AssertionError: assert #SBATCH --time=01:00:00 not in' the generated output and the second reporting the exec line 'agent ingest --record receipts --index watch-index.sqlite3' where the absolute path was asserted (review-base-source-head-tests.log, 2 failed, EXIT=1). The docstring's absolute-precision claim that did not hold for a relative argument: the same log quotes the base exec line carrying the bare '--record receipts'. All three are answered at head.

Independent verification. Four arms ran under the shared project interpreter in git-archive extractions of each revision under /tmp/rev-srw-ingest-133226907780, every log header naming the revision, the tree, the module under test as imported and the resolved working directory. Head arm at 5e1c4f2a: the node's declared two-file gate, 20 passed, exit 0 (review-head-gate.log). Base arm at 7774c689: the same two files, 19 passed, exit 0 (review-base-gate.log), so the run adds one test and no failing test by id or by count. Head arm, serving-interpreter parse guard: 1 passed, 8 deselected, exit 0 (review-head-serve-registry.log). Head arm, whole-tree ruff: 'All checks passed!' exit 0 (review-head-ruff.log). The reviewed run's own negative-control log was read against its declared string: the first line is byte-equal to 'removing --record and --index from the generated exec line must fail the embedded-paths test; applied as a scratch edit and restored', its two failed assertions carry the mutation marker --record-scratch-removed inside the generated exec line, it ends EXIT=1, and grep for that marker at head returns nothing, so no trace of the scratch edit survives in the commit.

One measurement of mine was wrong and is recorded because the same mistake is available to a reader. The first ruff pass in the scratch extraction reported 'Found 14 errors', all I001 import-sorting findings, none of them in a file this node touched. The instrument was at fault: the extraction carried imas_ambix, tests and pyproject.toml but not scripts/, and ruff's isort resolves first-party modules from the directories that exist. Re-extracting with scripts/ present, the same command over the same two directories prints 'All checks passed!'. A zero would have been the easy report; the check that mattered was to make the instrument see something known present.

What the change does not deliver. The node's declared write scope names five paths. Three were delivered. The figures directory is correctly unwritten, since the dispatch names no artifact. The fifth, docs/evidence/fragments/serving-record-warehouse/srw-ingest-service-lasts-and-names-its-paths.html, does not exist -- not at head 5e1c4f2a, not at the integrated HEAD 47225329, and not among the 18 fragments in that directory. The dispatch's landing contract says the fragment goes into the final commit, and every implement node that preceded this one in the plan wrote its own; the nearest comparable node, srw-watch-help-names-its-default, was dispatched with the identical sentence 'Your done-when names no artifact, so this node writes no figure and no evidence prose' and still wrote a 474-byte fragment. That sentence withholds the figure and the extended prose, not the anchor. The landing line still reaches the plan at promotion, so nothing is lost from the record -- what is missing is the node-level evidence anchor a reader follows from the plan to these gates.

One value is unpinned. The repair is guarded against the regression it repairs and not against a neighbouring one: tests/test_agent_ingest_cli.py:96 asserts the script's --time flows from _SUPPORTING_SERVICE_TIME_LIMIT and line 97 asserts 01:00:00 is absent, so reverting the generator to the finite limit fails. But no assertion anywhere in the tree states that _SUPPORTING_SERVICE_TIME_LIMIT is '0', so an edit of the shared constant to a finite value would leave both assertions green while ending the ingest, the router and the lane refresher on the scheduled reclaim the node's own commit message rejects. That is the repo's existing idiom for the other two services rather than a defect this node introduced, which is why it is recorded and scored rather than reported as a blocker.

The record itself. The manifest is complete: status complete, one commit, three changed paths, three gate results that match my re-runs, and a negative-control log named as a bare path. Its one fidelity gap is in the logs rather than the manifest. All three gate logs were written between 15:26:31 and 15:28:08 and the commit was made at 15:29:03, so each log's first line names rev=7774c68974b451d9e5b583900f184bbcdfdf6c61 -- the worktree's HEAD at the time, which was the base, because no commit contained the work yet. The header therefore identifies the tree and the commands but not the content revision, and a reader cannot tell from the log alone what was measured. This review closed that gap by re-running all three gates at 5e1c4f2a in a scratch extraction and recording the module path and working directory in each header.
